parts.part: citadel (acropolis or 'inner fort' in the south-west of the walled town)
parts.layout_phase: Period IC (transitional, 'proto-Harappan') in the excavator's final scheme (IAR 1986-87, 1987-88); Period II (Mature Indus) in his earlier reports (Bisht 1982; IAR 1983-84)
parts.what_was_built: In the scheme reached in the last two seasons, the citadel was created in Period IC, a transitional phase first separated in 1986-87 between the pre-Harappan Period I and the Mature Harappan Period II: 'The entire settlement was planned and constructed de novo. The dichotomous layout which the Harappans adopted was introduced during this sub-period. The fortification of the previous period was externally chiselled or partially sliced away and doubled in width for housing the citadel' (IAR 1986-87 p. 33). The final season confirmed that on three sides the builders of IC 'scrupulously followed the existing fortification wall albeit by widening it almost twice as large', and that Period II 'followed and maintained with marginal modifications at places the same planning', adding a flight of steps from the lower town to the acropolis (IAR 1987-88 p. 25). The wall reused was the Period IB defence, itself a rebuild to 2.5-3.5 m of an original 1.40 m wall (p. 23). Bisht's earlier account dates the citadel to Period II, when 'the full-bloomed Indus Culture makes its appearance': a fortified acropolis on ground raised by the Pre-Indus debris, its walls 5.4 to 7 m wide with squarish bastions, a postern with a built-in drain beside the north-eastern bastion and a brick ramp across the northern arm (1982 pp. 116-117); IAR 1983-84 (p. 27) describes the 'bipartite wall' that fortified the acropolis and divided the settlement into two halves. Period II had five or six building phases in 4.5 m of deposit, through which 'the original layout of the town was maintained most zealously' (Bisht 1982 pp. 118, 120).
parts.excavator_basis: Radiocarbon with a stratigraphic extrapolation, for Period II only: from two consistent PRL dates for the upper middle levels (1960 and 1980 B.C. on the 5730-year half-life, uncalibrated) Bisht writes: 'If one assigns the date of ca. 1800/1750 B.C. to the final phase, the beginning might be dated to about 2300 B.C. or so' (1982 p. 120). No date range was published for Period IC, which in the later scheme is the layout phase, or for Period I.

syntheses.statement: With calibrated values of 2283, 2278/2234/2209, 1523 and 1406 BC for the four Mature Harappan dates, Lal concludes that Banawali 'may have been a late contemporary of Kalibangan and may have even outlived it'; there are no dates for the pre-Harappan levels.
syntheses.disagreement: Lal sets the Banawali dates against a Kalibangan Period II starting c. 2550 BC; the Banawali dates come from the upper middle levels and do not date the start of the layout, which neither Bisht nor Lal places before Kalibangan's.

syntheses.statement: Summarising IAR 1986-87, Lal notes that the settlement was fortified only in Subperiod IB, that the citadel and lower town came into being in IC with continuity from Period I to II, that Banawali thus 'bridges the gap' seen between Periods I and II at Kalibangan, that there are no radiocarbon dates for Period I, and that Banawali 'continued its journey well into the Mature Harappan times'.

parts.conflicts: The excavator changed the phase of the layout. Bisht (1982 p. 116) saw only a 'seemingly transitional phase' about 50 cm thick, to be left 'a shadowy entity' pending more work, and dated the citadel and town to Period II; IAR 1983-84 (p. 26) still has Period II beginning 'with its unique town-planning'. From 1986-87 the citadel, the lower town and their 4:2:1 bricks are assigned to a new Period IC (IAR 1986-87 p. 33; IAR 1987-88 p. 25). Likewise Bisht (1982 p. 116; 1984 p. 90) had no positive evidence of a pre-Harappan fortification and suspected one under the Harappan wall, which the 1983-84 and later seasons exposed as the Period IB defence. The radiocarbon records disagree in detail: Bisht prints PRL-203 as 'PRL-205' with ±160; IAR 1975-76 gives PRL-203 ±100 on 5730 against ±150 on 5568 in PRL-II; IAR 1975-76 prints PRL-207 as 3910±110 with '(1240 B.C.)', inconsistent with itself and with PRL-II's 3100±100; and Bisht rejects PRL-204, labelled Harappa culture in the lists, as contaminated or from a later kiln. All four dates are from Period II above its middle; none comes from Period IC or Period I, so the start of the layout is undated by radiocarbon.

parts.part: lower town (outer walled town to the east and north of the citadel, with radial or semi-radial streets)
parts.layout_phase: Period IC (transitional) in the excavator's final scheme (IAR 1986-87, 1987-88); Period II in his earlier reports (Bisht 1982; IAR 1983-84)
parts.what_was_built: In Period IC 'the lower town was laid out contiguously towards the east as well as the north', with some IC house walls outside the general fortification in the east (IAR 1986-87 p. 33). The final season concluded that 'the outer fortification which was used and rebuilt by the Mature Harappan as well was in fact conceived and constructed during this phase', that it was 'more or less irregular trapezium in outline', and that 'the radial arrangement of streets of the lower division came into being due to the curvilinear nature of the antecedent fortification which was ... fully reappropriated during Period IC' (IAR 1987-88 p. 25). The earlier view was that 'Period II made its beginning with its unique town-planning which, besides appropriating, perhaps the entire antecedent settlement, extended its area nearly twice as large' (IAR 1983-84 p. 26); that season traced the northern town wall 275 m from corner to corner, a moat 6 m wide and 3.3 m deep beyond a berm, an eastern gate-complex and a 'radial or semi-radial system of streets' (pp. 26-27). The moat outside the eastern wall 'seems to be cut through in the middle of this phase', i.e. Period II (IAR 1987-88 pp. 25-27). Bisht (1982 pp. 116-117) describes major roads on both sides of the citadel wall and along the inner side of the town wall, with rows of house-blocks between longitudinal roads and narrow cross-alleys; in 1984 (p. 91) he stresses that 'the roads are neither always straight nor do they necessarily cut each other at right angles'.
parts.locator: iar1986-87 p. 33; iar1987-88 pp. 25-27; iar1983-84 pp. 26-27; bisht1982banawali pp. 116-117; bisht1984banawali p. 91
parts.excavator_basis: As for the citadel: Bisht's estimate for Period II, about 2300 B.C. to ca. 1800/1750 B.C., from two uncalibrated 5730-based dates for the upper middle levels and the count of building phases (1982 p. 120). Nothing is dated in the lower town itself.
parts.conflicts: The same change of scheme applies as for the citadel: Period II in 1982 and 1983-84, Period IC from 1986-87. No radiocarbon sample is attributed to the lower town; the four PRL dates are listed under the citadel part, where Bisht relates the three ZB1 samples to the citadel wall, and trench ZC2 (PRL-207) is not located in the sources we read.

parts.part: pre-Harappan walled settlement (Period IB), reused by the citadel
parts.what_was_built: The pre-Harappans first lived in an open settlement (IA) and then enclosed it with a mud-brick wall (IB) (IAR 1986-87 p. 32). In the well-documented trench the second stage 'began with the introduction of a fortification, delimiting the habitation', represented by 1.60 m of debris coinciding with 'the first two building phases of the defensive wall' (IAR 1983-84 p. 24). The final season describes two major constructional phases: a wall originally 1.40 m wide, augmented by an inner dwarf wall when it began to tilt, then rebuilt as a massive wall now 2.50-3.20 m wide (3.50 m at one point), probably 'designed like a large oval following the existing natural elevation', with five phases of houses of 3:2:1 bricks and a 1.40 m street kept along its inner side (IAR 1987-88 pp. 23-25).
parts.excavator_basis: No date range or radiocarbon determination has been published for Period I (Lal 1997 p. 245; Lal 2003 p. 29).
parts.conflicts: Bisht (1982 p. 116; 1984 p. 90) reported no positive evidence of a pre-Harappan fortification; it was found from 1983-84 onwards. Lal (2003 p. 29) notes that no wall is ascribable to IA.

first_occupation.phase: Period IA (pre-Harappan, Kalibangan culture, 'pre-defence phase'): an open settlement on natural soil
first_occupation.basis: No radiocarbon dates and no excavator's date range for Period I (Lal 1997 p. 245; Lal 2003 p. 29). IAR 1987-88 (p. 23) gives IA an average 0.60 m deposit with one structural phase and a fired-brick structure resting on natural soil.
first_occupation.locator: iar1987-88 p. 23; iar1986-87 p. 32; bisht1982banawali p. 115; lal2003kalibangan p. 29

notes: Banawali (Banawali Sottar, District Hissar, now Fatehabad) was excavated by the Department of Archaeology and Museums, Haryana, in 1974-77 (reported by R. S. Bisht) and by the Archaeological Survey of India under Bisht in 1983-84, 1986-87 and 1987-88; no final report has been published, so the account rests on Bisht's 1982 and 1984 chapters and the IAR summaries. The excavator's sequence grew from three periods (I pre-Harappan, II Mature Indus, III post-Harappan; Bisht 1982 p. 115) to I A (open settlement), I B (defended), I C (transitional, 'proto-Harappan'), II and III (IAR 1987-88 p. 23). In the final scheme the walled citadel, the walled lower town and the street plan are works of Period IC, built on and around the Period IB wall and kept by Period II; we therefore give both the IC and the Period II attribution for each part and record the IB enclosure as a separate part. Only four radiocarbon determinations exist, all on samples from Period II above its middle levels, published by the Physical Research Laboratory (PRL-II, 5568 half-life) and reprinted on the 5730 half-life in IAR 1974-75 and 1975-76 and by Bisht 1982; Lal 1997 gives calibrated values. None dates Period IC or Period I, and no Bayesian model exists. We could not obtain Bisht 1978 ('Banawali: a new Harappan site in Haryana', Man and Environment 2; no copy of that volume found on archive.org, which holds vol. 1 and vols. 13 onwards), Bisht 1987 in Pande and Chattopadhyaya (eds), Archaeology and History: Essays in Memory of Shri A. Ghosh (not found online), Bisht and Asthana 1979, the cyclostyled PRL date lists Bisht cites, the 1993 second edition of Possehl's Harappan Civilization, or Possehl's compilations (The Indus Civilization, 2002, is lending-restricted on archive.org). IAR 1984-85 (p. 253, conservation of excavated structures) and 1985-86 (exploration) were checked and add nothing on dating. The IAR volumes read are re-typeset ASI editions; one printed value (PRL-207 in IAR 1975-76) looks like a transcription error.
